spec.title: Answers per second by class (k6)
spec.description: Per run, split by variant (unset = no deadlines, set = 2 s pool wait + 5 s statement) and fault (lat, stall). 202 = accepted, 503 = fast refusal, hung = status 0, no answer before the k6 timeout (15 s). Expected with deadlines: 503 instead of hung. Surprising: any hung line in a 'set' run. k6_b10_resp_* counters are ADDED BY B10 (exist after the first k6 run); k6 series linger after a run ends.

spec.title: Client latency p50 and p99 (k6)
spec.description: How long k6 waited, including requests that timed out at 15 s (a hung request is recorded with its full timeout, so p99 flat at 15 s means many requests hung). With deadlines p99 should stay near 2 s (pool wait) to 5 s (statement).

spec.title: Offered vs accepted (k6)
spec.description: Offered = every request k6 sent per second, accepted = 202 per second. The gap is everything that failed or hung. lat runs offer 180/s, stall runs 100/s.

spec.title: Requests waiting for a pool connection
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_waiting: requests queued inside the Node process for one of the 25 connections. Without the pool wait deadline it can grow without a bound (about 58/s in lat, about 100/s during the stall). With the deadline it should stop growing near offered rate x 2 s. Surprising: a queue that keeps shrinking by itself during a fault.

spec.title: Pool connections: total, idle, max
spec.description: In a stall all connections are busy (idle = 0) while they wait for the table lock. total should sit at the pool max (25).

spec.title: HTTP requests in flight (server)
spec.description: http_requests_in_flight: requests the server has accepted and not answered. This is what pile up in memory. With no deadlines it keeps rising and it falls only when the database answers; clients that left are still counted here.

spec.title: Server memory
spec.description: RSS and V8 heap in use, plus external memory (Buffers: the request bodies live here). Queued requests hold their body, so growth should follow the queue; the stall runs use a 20 KB filler to make it visible. Heap does not shrink right after the queue drains (garbage collection), so compare the peak, not the end.

spec.title: Pool wait time p99 (server)
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_wait_seconds: time a request spent waiting for a connection before it got one. Requests that never get one (pool timeout) are not recorded here, they show up as pool_timeout errors below. With a 2 s deadline this should be capped near 2 s.

spec.title: Database errors by type
spec.description: pool_timeout = waited longer than the pool wait deadline; statement_timeout = Postgres cancelled the statement after 5 s. Both should be zero in 'unset' runs (there is no deadline that could fire).

spec.title: Server answers by status
spec.description: What the server itself sent per second, from the server's own counter (not k6). A 202 here for a client that already left is wasted work. /metrics scrapes excluded.

spec.title: Events inserted per second
spec.description: ep_events_inserted_total: rows the server committed. After k6 stops (or after the lock ends) rows can still be inserted for requests whose clients timed out. That is work nobody reads.

spec.title: Statement time p99 (server)
spec.description: ep_pg_query_duration_seconds: time of the INSERT as seen by the server. In the stall it should reach 5 s with deadlines (cancelled) and the length of the lock without.

spec.title: Server process CPU (user and system)
spec.description: In cores. Hung requests cost almost no CPU while they wait; a drain after the fault is a burst. Pinned to 2 CPUs, so 2.0 is the ceiling.

spec.title: Pinned CPUs busy: server, postgres
spec.description: Host CPU busy share on the pinned CPUs (1 - idle). Postgres should be nearly idle while the table lock is held: it is waiting, not working.

spec.title: Postgres container CPU
spec.description: ep_pg_container_cpu_seconds_total rate, in cores (from infra/scripts/pg-container-exporter.sh, started by run.sh).

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations
spec.description: Must stay 0. A dropped iteration means k6 ran out of VUs (rate x timeout too big) and the offered rate was not delivered; discard that run.

spec.title: k6 VUs in use
spec.description: Each hung request holds one VU for the full 15 s timeout, so VUs ~ rate x 15 s at most (2700 for lat, 1500 for stall). The limit is 4000.

spec.title: k6 pinned CPUs busy
spec.description: Generator headroom. Keep under about 70%.

spec.title: Event loop lag p99 (server)
spec.description: nodejs_eventloop_lag_p99_seconds. A large value means the Node process itself is slow, which would blur the timeout effect.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: do requests hang or fail fast?

spec.description: CPU ids the server group is pinned to (0,6), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_server"

spec.name: cpu_k6

spec.description: CPU ids the k6 group is pinned to (3,9,4,10), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_k6"
